missing: Outage-specific runtime math: how many hours each unit actually keeps a fridge, furnace blower or CPAP running, how realistic solar recharge is during a multi-day grey-sky outage, and what a transfer-switch setup adds in cost; plus current prices and discount codes across the picks.
why: Four major reviewers with their own testing answer this exact question: Consumer Reports lab-tested six station-plus-panel kits for outage use, OutdoorGearLab tested 14 with measured usable capacity and a home-backup pick, Popular Mechanics and Good Housekeeping both run tested roundups with blackout picks, and TechRadar adds a rated comparison table. The remaining slots are a niche home-backup roundup and an outage-data site. A new Dealectric page would be competing against CR and OutdoorGearLab head-on for a broad, untargeted question; this is not an opening.
